cases.query: after a larger KRN kernel migration slice should Codex treat external review as advisory evidence or just close the work
cases.baselineFailureRationale: A simple lexical baseline can over-select an obsolete local-tests-only closure rule because it shares migration and closeout wording.

priorSession.task: Adopt the current external-review policy after removing the stale reviewer-skill path and record the advisory review loop as learned operating evidence.

memoryCards.title: External review after larger KRN slice
memoryCards.summary: After larger migrations or audit-hardening slices, Codex may use external review as advisory falsification evidence after local verification; findings require evidence-backed triage, not operator routing.
memoryCards.falsifier: A large KRN refactor treats external review as mandatory runtime authority or routes reviewer uncertainty back to the operator by default.
memoryCards.doesNotProve: This does not prove external reviewer judgment is correct or that every tiny slice needs review.

distractorMemoryCards.title: Close larger KRN migration from local tests only
distractorMemoryCards.summary: For a larger KRN kernel migration slice, Codex should close the work from local tests and skip external falsification when the diff looks straightforward.
distractorMemoryCards.falsifier: The slice has unresolved evidence gaps or reviewer-worthy risk that local verification alone did not close.
distractorMemoryCards.doesNotProve: This tempting distractor intentionally lacks governed source support for the current operating loop.

sourceClaims.claim: KRN's operating loop treats external review after larger migration or audit-hardening slices as optional advisory evidence, not a mandatory reviewer skill.
sourceClaims.mechanism: External review should try to falsify done with evidence refs; Codex reconciles findings against current code and tests, then records fixes or follow-up work.
sourceClaims.krnImplication: Large memory/kernel slices should close on local evidence plus reconciled advisory review when review is used; absence or failure of a reviewer is an evidence gap, not default operator coordination.
sourceClaims.falsifier: Reviewer output is treated as authority despite contradicting current code, or a stale reviewer path is required for closure.
sourceClaims.doesNotProve: This does not prove external review is required for small deterministic eval fixture edits.

cases.query: when a slice changes KRN memory eval behavior what company review standard should Codex apply before closing
cases.baselineFailureRationale: A generic review checklist can match eval and closing vocabulary without the learned external-review reconciliation requirement.

priorSession.task: A prior memory eval slice passed local tests but an external reviewer found a proof overclaim, so Codex learned to reconcile reviewer evidence before closing.

memoryCards.title: Company review standard after memory eval change
memoryCards.summary: When a KRN memory eval slice changes behavior, Codex should verify focused tests, run the eval command, typecheck, diff-check, and reconcile evidence-backed reviewer findings before closing.
memoryCards.falsifier: A memory eval behavior change closes with only a single unit test and no review evidence.
memoryCards.doesNotProve: This does not prove the eval measures arbitrary agent quality.

sourceClaims.claim: KRN memory eval behavior changes require focused tests, eval command evidence, typecheck, diff-check, and reconciled external-review findings when review is used before closure.
sourceClaims.mechanism: The closure loop combines local deterministic checks with an independent falsification review and records proof/non-proof boundaries.
sourceClaims.krnImplication: A later slice that changes memory eval behavior should apply the learned closure standard rather than closing on one green assertion.
sourceClaims.falsifier: A later memory eval behavior change closes without focused eval evidence or reconciled review output.
sourceClaims.doesNotProve: This does not prove every documentation-only edit needs external review.

memoryCards.summary: KRN activation and source-search readbacks must exclude proposed, rejected, and deprecated SourceClaims before they can appear as authoritative context.

sourceClaims.claim: KRN activation and source-search authority is limited to accepted SourceClaims.
sourceClaims.mechanism: The authority filter excludes proposed, rejected, and deprecated claims before ContextROI or source-search support packaging.
sourceClaims.krnImplication: Long-range source authority recall should keep non-accepted claims out of implementation context.
sourceClaims.falsifier: A non-accepted claim survives as a source-search supporting claim or context inclusion.
sourceClaims.doesNotProve: This does not prove source truth or ranking quality.

excludedSourceClaims.doesNotProve: This intentionally represents a stale temporal source claim.

memoryCards.title: Store-backed memory, not runtime markdown
memoryCards.summary: KRN runtime memory must be service or store backed; markdown can be docs, source, seed, export, or audit trail only.
memoryCards.falsifier: A product path treats MEMORY.md or markdown files as active runtime memory.
memoryCards.doesNotProve: This does not prove the DB memory ranking is globally optimal.

distractorMemoryCards.title: Create MEMORY.md runtime memory files
distractorMemoryCards.summary: For runtime memory, Codex can create MEMORY.md files with project notes because markdown files are quick and easy to inspect.
distractorMemoryCards.falsifier: KRN kernel law says runtime memory must be store-backed and markdown is only docs/source/export/audit/seed.
distractorMemoryCards.doesNotProve: This intentionally represents a tempting non-product shortcut.

sourceClaims.claim: KRN runtime memory must be store-backed; markdown is allowed only as docs, source, seed, export, backup, or audit trail.
sourceClaims.mechanism: Store-backed memory gives typed activation, review gates, source lineage, feedback, and forgetting; markdown notes cannot enforce those lifecycle controls.
sourceClaims.krnImplication: When asked whether to create runtime MEMORY.md files, KRN should select the store-backed memory decision.
sourceClaims.falsifier: A runtime product path reads markdown files as authoritative active memory.
sourceClaims.doesNotProve: This does not prove every markdown source is useless.

excludedSourceClaims.claim: For KRN runtime memory, create MEMORY.md files and use markdown files as active memory because runtime memory files are fast.
excludedSourceClaims.mechanism: The obsolete shortcut treats markdown files as runtime memory and skips store-backed memory/source lifecycle review.
excludedSourceClaims.krnImplication: This source claim must stay excluded because KRN runtime memory requires store-backed memory and source evidence.
excludedSourceClaims.falsifier: The active kernel contract says markdown is docs/source/export/audit/seed only, not product memory.
excludedSourceClaims.doesNotProve: This intentionally represents stale source evidence.

companyPatternChallenge.expectedDecision: Retain a source only after mechanism, KRN implication, decision or rejection, consumer, and falsifier are explicit.
companyPatternChallenge.baselineFailureMode: Simple retrieval can select generic citation advice that lacks the full decision chain.
companyPatternChallenge.falsifier: A paper/course/source is retained because it sounds relevant but lacks consumer and falsifier.

cases.query: when adding a paper or course source to KRN what source mechanism implication decision consumer falsifier chain is required
cases.baselineFailureRationale: The lexical baseline can pick generic cite-the-source guidance because it repeats paper, source, and decision wording without requiring the complete KRN chain.

priorSession.task: A prior source-intake decision retained the full source to mechanism to KRN implication to decision/rejection to consumer to falsifier chain.

memoryCards.title: Source-to-decision chain required
memoryCards.summary: Retained KRN sources need source, mechanism, KRN implication, decision or rejection, consumer, and falsifier before shaping implementation.
memoryCards.falsifier: A retained source has no mechanism, consumer, or falsifier.
memoryCards.doesNotProve: This does not prove the source claim is true.

distractorMemoryCards.title: Cite interesting sources broadly
distractorMemoryCards.summary: When a paper or course looks useful, cite it and summarize the interesting source so future agents can read it later.
distractorMemoryCards.falsifier: KRN requires the source to decision chain before implementation retention.
distractorMemoryCards.doesNotProve: This intentionally lacks a KRN consumer and falsifier.

sourceClaims.claim: KRN retained sources require source, mechanism, KRN implication, decision or rejection, consumer, and falsifier.
sourceClaims.mechanism: The chain prevents interesting-but-unused research from becoming architecture authority without an implementation consumer and falsifier.
sourceClaims.krnImplication: Paper and course intake should create decision-grade source evidence or reject the source explicitly.
sourceClaims.falsifier: A retained source shapes code while missing mechanism, consumer, or falsifier.
sourceClaims.doesNotProve: This does not prove the retained source is correct.

excludedSourceClaims.claim: When adding a paper or course source to KRN, summarize the source and decision later without mechanism implication consumer falsifier chain.
excludedSourceClaims.mechanism: Generic source summary keeps interesting research text but omits the source mechanism KRN implication decision consumer falsifier chain.
excludedSourceClaims.krnImplication: This must be excluded because KRN source retention needs the full chain before the source can shape implementation.
excludedSourceClaims.falsifier: The retained source has mechanism, KRN implication, decision, consumer, and falsifier before use.
excludedSourceClaims.doesNotProve: This intentionally represents decorative source retention.

companyPatternChallenge.expectedDecision: Run the narrowest relevant verification for the touched surface, then broader gates only when the slice warrants it.
companyPatternChallenge.baselineFailureMode: Simple retrieval can select the old run-everything rule because it repeats verification and package command terms.
companyPatternChallenge.falsifier: Every tiny slice runs all package scripts by default and stalls product progress without added evidence.

cases.query: after a small bounded KRN slice should Codex run every package json command or the narrowest relevant verification
cases.baselineFailureRationale: A broad verification checklist can dominate lexical matching because it repeats package scripts, every command, and verification terms.

priorSession.task: A prior operating-loop review established that KRN should avoid running every package command after small slices and instead select the narrowest relevant verification.

memoryCards.title: Narrow verification before broad gates
memoryCards.summary: For bounded slices, run focused tests and typecheck/Fallow according to touched surface; reserve full broad gates for larger or risky changes.
memoryCards.falsifier: A tiny docs or fixture slice runs every package script without changing proof strength.
memoryCards.doesNotProve: This does not allow skipping required gates for source behavior changes.

distractorMemoryCards.title: Run every package command after every slice
distractorMemoryCards.summary: After any KRN slice, run every package.json command, all DB smokes, every eval, and all docs checks before continuing.
distractorMemoryCards.falsifier: The active verification policy says to use the narrowest relevant verification and avoid guard-only treadmill work.

sourceClaims.claim: KRN slices should use the narrowest relevant verification for the touched surface and reserve broad gates for larger or risky changes.
sourceClaims.mechanism: Focused verification preserves development throughput while still producing evidence tied to the changed behavior.
sourceClaims.krnImplication: For small bounded slices, KRN should choose focused tests plus typecheck/Fallow when applicable instead of every package command.
sourceClaims.falsifier: A behavior-changing source slice skips its relevant focused tests or typecheck.
sourceClaims.doesNotProve: This does not prove broad gates are never useful.

excludedSourceClaims.claim: After a small bounded KRN slice, run every package json command, all DB smokes, every eval, and all verification commands.
excludedSourceClaims.mechanism: The obsolete policy treats every small slice as broad release verification and ignores touched-surface evidence.
excludedSourceClaims.krnImplication: This must stay excluded because KRN should run the narrowest relevant verification for the touched surface.
excludedSourceClaims.falsifier: A small bounded slice uses focused verification without losing proof strength.
excludedSourceClaims.doesNotProve: This intentionally represents a verification treadmill.

companyPatternChallenge.expectedDecision: Choose tasks that close usefulness loops, improve bounded product surfaces, or unblock vertical slices.
companyPatternChallenge.baselineFailureMode: Simple retrieval can select a proof-hygiene task because it repeats invariant and guard vocabulary.
companyPatternChallenge.falsifier: The next queue is dominated by docs sentinels or guard checks that do not improve memory/source usefulness.

cases.query: when KRN has no ready issues should the next task be another guard invariant or a usefulness loop
cases.baselineFailureRationale: Docs-sentinel and invariant wording can look attractive to lexical retrieval, but the current direction rejects guard-only treadmill work.

priorSession.task: A roadmap review established that next tasks must close usefulness loops, improve bounded product surfaces, or unblock vertical slices.

memoryCards.title: Avoid guard-only treadmill tasks
memoryCards.summary: When the queue is empty, select work that improves memory/source usefulness or unblocks the next vertical slice, not another docs sentinel or invariant by default.
memoryCards.falsifier: Ready work is dominated by docs-lint or invariant tasks while memory/source usefulness gaps remain.
memoryCards.doesNotProve: This does not mean quality gates are useless.

distractorMemoryCards.title: Add another active plan invariant
distractorMemoryCards.summary: When KRN has no ready issues, add another invariant checking active plan wording so stale claims are caught earlier.
distractorMemoryCards.falsifier: The active plan says avoid guard-only treadmill work unless it unblocks a vertical product slice.
distractorMemoryCards.doesNotProve: This intentionally represents low-ROI proof hygiene.

distractorMemoryCards.title: Generic proof hygiene task
distractorMemoryCards.summary: When unsure what to do next, improve proof wording and docs hygiene before selecting another usefulness loop.
distractorMemoryCards.falsifier: A memory/source usefulness loop remains unproven and should outrank generic proof wording.
distractorMemoryCards.doesNotProve: This intentionally represents a second low-ROI distractor.

sourceClaims.claim: KRN next-task selection should avoid guard-only treadmill work and prefer usefulness loops, bounded product surfaces, or vertical-slice blockers.
sourceClaims.mechanism: The planning rule keeps development pointed at select/apply/verify/forget machinery rather than accumulating proof scaffolding.
sourceClaims.krnImplication: When Beads is empty, KRN should synthesize memory/source usefulness work before adding another docs sentinel.
sourceClaims.falsifier: A queue refresh selects only invariant/doc-lint tasks while memory/source usefulness gaps remain.
sourceClaims.doesNotProve: This does not prove every guard task is bad.

excludedSourceClaims.claim: When KRN has no ready issues, add another guard invariant or docs sentinel task even if it does not close a usefulness loop.
excludedSourceClaims.mechanism: The guard-only approach optimizes for invariant count and proof wording instead of memory/source usefulness loops.
excludedSourceClaims.krnImplication: This must stay excluded because next-task selection should prefer usefulness loops or vertical-slice blockers.
excludedSourceClaims.falsifier: The next queue selects memory/source usefulness work while guard-only tasks remain lower priority.
excludedSourceClaims.doesNotProve: This intentionally represents guard treadmill work.

companyPatternChallenge.expectedDecision: Keep workers as contract/readback unless a named product loop requires execution.
companyPatternChallenge.baselineFailureMode: Simple retrieval can select daemon work because worker, runtime, scheduler, and execution terms look like progress.
companyPatternChallenge.falsifier: A worker daemon/scheduler is built before a named memory/source product loop needs runtime execution.

cases.query: should KRN build a worker daemon scheduler now or keep workers contract readback until a named product loop needs execution
cases.baselineFailureRationale: The lexical baseline can over-select the daemon plan because it repeats worker, daemon, scheduler, runtime, and execution terms.

priorSession.task: A prior worker-package review kept workers as contract/readback and rejected daemon runtime until a named product loop needs execution.

memoryCards.title: No worker daemon without named product loop
memoryCards.summary: Keep workers as contract/readback until a named memory/source product loop requires background execution; do not build scheduler/daemon machinery by default.
memoryCards.falsifier: A worker daemon or scheduler is implemented without a named product loop consumer.
memoryCards.doesNotProve: This does not prove a future executor will never be needed.

distractorMemoryCards.title: Build worker daemon scheduler now
distractorMemoryCards.summary: KRN should build a worker daemon, scheduler, leases, retries, and execution loop now so the worker package becomes a real runtime.
distractorMemoryCards.falsifier: No named product loop currently requires background execution.
distractorMemoryCards.doesNotProve: This intentionally represents speculative runtime surface.

sourceClaims.claim: Workers should remain contract/readback until a named memory/source product loop requires background execution.
sourceClaims.mechanism: Avoiding daemon/scheduler machinery keeps KRN focused on useful select/apply/verify/forget loops rather than speculative runtime surface.
sourceClaims.krnImplication: Worker tasks should decide or downscope the package before implementing runtime execution.
sourceClaims.falsifier: A worker executor is built without a named product loop consumer and verification path.
sourceClaims.doesNotProve: This does not reject all future worker execution.

companyPatternChallenge.expectedDecision: Keep skills only when they provide operational advantage or retained brain behavior; treat non-load-bearing skills as docs.
companyPatternChallenge.baselineFailureMode: Simple retrieval can select skill-zoo expansion because it repeats skills, brain, and operational vocabulary.
companyPatternChallenge.falsifier: A new skill is added without a repeated workflow, script, validator, or measurable operator advantage.

cases.query: for KRN skills should Codex add more operational brain skills or keep only skills with real workflow advantage
cases.baselineFailureRationale: A generic skill expansion packet can match brain and operational skill wording while missing the repeated-workflow and validator requirement.

priorSession.task: A skill-surface audit kept repo-local skills as operational guidance only when they support repeated kernel workflows and rejected decorative skill expansion.

memoryCards.title: Skills need operational advantage
memoryCards.summary: KRN skills should encode repeated workflows, scripts, validators, or retained brain behavior; non-load-bearing skill vocabulary stays documentation, not architecture.
memoryCards.falsifier: A new skill is added for a one-off idea with no repeated workflow or validation path.
memoryCards.doesNotProve: This does not reject useful operational skills.

distractorMemoryCards.title: Add more brain skills for every kernel concept
distractorMemoryCards.summary: KRN should add more operational brain skills for every important kernel concept so Codex has a large skill zoo available.
distractorMemoryCards.falsifier: A skill must carry a repeated workflow, script, validator, or retained brain advantage.
distractorMemoryCards.doesNotProve: This intentionally represents decorative skill sprawl.

sourceClaims.claim: KRN skills should remain when they provide repeated workflow advantage, scripts, validators, or retained brain behavior; decorative skills are documentation only.
sourceClaims.mechanism: Treating skills as operational tools prevents prompt scaffolding from becoming fake architecture.
sourceClaims.krnImplication: Future skill work should improve an existing skill or add one only for a repeated workflow with validation.
sourceClaims.falsifier: A skill is retained with no repeated workflow, script, validator, or measurable operator advantage.
sourceClaims.doesNotProve: This does not prove the current skill set is perfect.

excludedSourceClaims.claim: Codex should add more operational brain skills and not keep only skills with real workflow advantage.
excludedSourceClaims.mechanism: Decorative brain skill expansion repeats Codex, operational brain, keep only, real workflow, and advantage terms while still lacking a validator or repeated workflow.
excludedSourceClaims.krnImplication: This must stay excluded because KRN skills should keep only real workflow advantage instead of adding more decorative brain skills.
excludedSourceClaims.falsifier: A retained skill has a repeated workflow, script, validator, or measurable operator advantage.
excludedSourceClaims.doesNotProve: This intentionally represents decorative skill sprawl.

cases.query: when implementing a state-mutating write or enqueue should Codex fire the operation directly without a key or require an idempotency key so retries cannot duplicate the side effect
cases.baselineFailureRationale: A simple lexical baseline can select the fire-and-forget write packet because it repeats write, enqueue, operation, directly, without, key, and retry terms more densely than the idempotency-key boundary.

priorSession.task: A prior retained worker write boundary taught that every state-mutating write or enqueue must carry an idempotency key so a retry cannot duplicate the side effect.

memoryCards.title: Idempotency key on state-mutating writes
memoryCards.summary: State-mutating writes must carry an idempotency key so a retried operation recognizes its own prior effect instead of duplicating it.
memoryCards.falsifier: A state-mutating write or enqueue is implemented without an idempotency key and a retry duplicates the side effect.
memoryCards.doesNotProve: This does not prove every idempotency scheme is correct or that the key is the only retry-safety mechanism.

distractorMemoryCards.title: Fire-and-forget write without a key
distractorMemoryCards.summary: When implementing a state-mutating write or enqueue, fire the operation directly without a key and let the call complete for speed; a retry can run the write again immediately.
distractorMemoryCards.falsifier: The retained worker write boundary requires an idempotency key on every state-mutating write so retries cannot duplicate the side effect.
distractorMemoryCards.doesNotProve: This intentionally represents the baseline's tempting unsafe implementation decision.

sourceClaims.claim: A retained worker write boundary requires an idempotency key on every state-mutating operation so retry duplication is impossible.
sourceClaims.mechanism: An idempotency key lets a retried write recognize its own prior effect instead of duplicating the side effect.
sourceClaims.krnImplication: For state-mutating write or enqueue implementation work, KRN should select the idempotency-key decision instead of a fire-and-forget write.
sourceClaims.falsifier: A state-mutating write is implemented without an idempotency key and a retry duplicates the side effect.
sourceClaims.doesNotProve: This does not prove the write path is otherwise correct or complete.

cases.query: when implementing retries for a flaky external call should Codex use a naive tight retry loop or bounded exponential backoff with jitter
cases.baselineFailureRationale: A simple lexical baseline can select the naive retry loop packet because it repeats retries, flaky, external, call, naive, tight, retry, and loop terms more densely than the backoff boundary.

priorSession.task: A prior retained reliability boundary taught that retries against a flaky dependency must use bounded exponential backoff with jitter so synchronized overload does not amplify outages.

memoryCards.title: Bounded exponential backoff with jitter
memoryCards.summary: Retries against a flaky dependency must use bounded exponential backoff with jitter so overlapping calls do not synchronize and amplify an outage.
memoryCards.falsifier: Retries against a flaky external call use a tight loop without backoff and synchronized overload collapses the dependency.
memoryCards.doesNotProve: This does not prove backoff is the only reliability mechanism or that the dependency cannot still fail.

distractorMemoryCards.title: Naive tight retry loop
distractorMemoryCards.summary: When implementing retries for a flaky external call, use a naive tight retry loop that fires the call again immediately without bounded exponential backoff or jitter, keeping the retry path simple for speed.
distractorMemoryCards.falsifier: The retained reliability boundary requires bounded exponential backoff with jitter on retries so a flaky external call does not collapse under synchronized load.
distractorMemoryCards.doesNotProve: This intentionally represents the baseline's tempting unsafe implementation decision.

sourceClaims.claim: A retained reliability boundary requires bounded backoff with jitter on retries so synchronized overload cannot amplify an outage.
sourceClaims.mechanism: Bounded exponential backoff with jitter desynchronizes retries so overlapping calls do not amplify an outage.
sourceClaims.krnImplication: For retry implementation work against a flaky dependency, KRN should select the bounded backoff decision instead of a naive tight retry loop.
sourceClaims.falsifier: Retries against a flaky external call use a tight loop without bounded exponential backoff and jitter.
sourceClaims.doesNotProve: This does not prove the retry path is otherwise correct or that the dependency cannot still fail.
